summary: A BBN list of the monthly preventive maintenance times for each IMP and TIP, mostly timed to match maintenance on the hosts at the same site. It says rescheduling would be announced through the TIP news and in notes to technical liaisons. Permanent changes would appear as RFCs.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC lists the monthly preventive maintenance times for IMPs and TIPs. It also explains how temporary and permanent schedule changes would be announced.

subtitle: A monthly schedule for preventive maintenance on IMPs and TIPs.

tldr.problem: The network needed a published schedule for regular preventive maintenance on IMPs and TIPs.
tldr.mechanism: BBN lists maintenance windows by week and day of the month, with each time given in Eastern Time.
tldr.outcome: The notice explains how schedule changes would be announced and provides the current maintenance timetable.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 445's status as Unknown. The RFC records an operational maintenance schedule.

sections.title: A Monthly Maintenance Schedule
sections.content:
RFC 445 presents the current preventive maintenance schedule for network IMPs and TIPs. A machine is normally scheduled at the same time each month, and the schedule tries to match maintenance on hosts at the same site.

All listed times are Eastern Time. The schedule is grouped by week and weekday.
sections.plainLanguage: Network equipment has a planned maintenance window each month. The schedule tries to align it with host maintenance at the same site.

sections.title: When a Schedule Changes
sections.content:
The RFC says maintenance may need to be rescheduled because of network connectivity or other reasons. Such changes would be announced as soon as possible through TIP NEWS and a Journal note to Technical Liaisons.

Permanent changes to the schedule would be announced through the RFC process.
sections.plainLanguage: Temporary changes would be announced through TIP NEWS and a Journal note. Permanent schedule changes would be announced in an RFC.

sections.title: Maintenance Windows by Site
sections.content:
The list assigns sites and equipment to recurring windows such as the first Monday, second Wednesday, or fourth Thursday of each month. It includes separate entries for some sites' IMPs and TIPs.

The RFC presents the timetable as the current schedule, rather than specifying a maintenance protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The table says which network machines are scheduled on each week and weekday. It is an operations notice, not a technical protocol.
